# Agent Taskbay

Factual summary of the repository at the current checkout. The console package on npm is `agent-taskbay` 1.0.0. Features listed under Unreleased in CHANGELOG.md are in the source tree and are not in that npm release until a later release says so. Prefer the docs in `docs/` when this file and a doc disagree; the code is the authority.

Agent Taskbay is a self-hosted console for A2A agents. People start work, follow it after closing the browser, answer questions, and approve specific actions. Taskbay does not run the agents. It is an A2A client: the web process writes commands, workers send them, and the screens read the database.

Created and maintained by Shashi Kanth G S, part of Allsrc. MIT license. It has not had an independent security review.

## Run it

Node.js 22.19 or newer.

```bash
npx agent-taskbay
```

Console: `http://127.0.0.1:3002`. Embedded database: `~/.agent-taskbay`. Local mode signs everyone in as an administrator and listens on loopback only.

```bash
npx agent-taskbay demo-agent
```

Five fixture cards on port 4010:

1. `http://127.0.0.1:4010/showcase/card.json` — form, A2UI, and an approval request
2. `http://127.0.0.1:4010/form/card.json` — structured form
3. `http://127.0.0.1:4010/approver/card.json` — approval request
4. `http://127.0.0.1:4010/a2ui/card.json` — A2UI surface
5. `http://127.0.0.1:4010/automation/card.json` — tasks started outside the console

There is no echo agent and no error agent in that command.

## Protocol

The gateway uses `@a2a-js/sdk`. It speaks JSON-RPC and HTTP+JSON. It does not speak gRPC.

Agent Card discovery reads `/.well-known/agent-card.json` when the URL you give does not itself end in `.json`. A v1 card is recognized by `supportedInterfaces`. A v0.3 card (a `url` field or protocol version 0.3) is normalized and has not been verified against real v0.3 agents.

Extension entries are objects: `{ "uri", "required", "params"? }`. These URIs are defined by this project only. They are not A2A standards.

| Extension | URI |
| --- | --- |
| Structured form | `https://extensions.allsrc.dev/agent-taskbay/structured-form/v1` |
| Approval request | `https://extensions.allsrc.dev/agent-taskbay/approval-request/v1` |
| Skill routing | `https://extensions.allsrc.dev/agent-taskbay/skill-routing/v1` |
| A2UI v0.9 (external) | `https://a2ui.org/a2a-extension/a2ui/v0.9` |

```json
{
  "name": "Database migration agent",
  "description": "Asks a person before applying a migration.",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "supportedInterfaces": [
    {
      "url": "http://127.0.0.1:5050/a2a",
      "protocolBinding": "JSONRPC",
      "protocolVersion": "1.0"
    }
  ],
  "capabilities": {
    "streaming": false,
    "pushNotifications": false,
    "extensions": [
      { "uri": "https://extensions.allsrc.dev/agent-taskbay/approval-request/v1", "required": false }
    ]
  },
  "defaultInputModes": ["text/plain", "application/json"],
  "defaultOutputModes": ["text/plain", "application/json"],
  "skills": [
    { "id": "migrate", "name": "Migrate", "description": "Propose a schema migration." }
  ]
}
```

## Task states

Wire values look like `TASK_STATE_SUBMITTED`, `TASK_STATE_WORKING`, `TASK_STATE_INPUT_REQUIRED`, `TASK_STATE_AUTH_REQUIRED`, `TASK_STATE_COMPLETED`, `TASK_STATE_FAILED`, `TASK_STATE_CANCELED`, and `TASK_STATE_REJECTED`.

`TASK_STATE_AUTH_REQUIRED` means the agent needs credentials. Taskbay displays it. The person authorizes outside Taskbay and replies to resume. It is not an approval.

Approvals use `TASK_STATE_INPUT_REQUIRED` and a data part on the status message:

```json
{
  "data": {
    "title": "Delete the staging cluster",
    "summary": "Removes all staging nodes and volumes.",
    "risk": "high",
    "expiresInSeconds": 3600,
    "action": { "kind": "send_message", "text": "Approved. Delete the staging cluster." }
  },
  "mediaType": "application/vnd.agent-taskbay.approval-request+json"
}
```

| Field | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| `title` | Required. 1 to 300 characters. |
| `summary` | Optional. At most 4000 characters. |
| `risk` | `low`, `medium` (default), or `high`. |
| `expiresInSeconds` | Optional. Clamped to 5 minutes through 7 days. Default 24 hours. |
| `action` | `send_message` with `text` (and optional `data`), or `send_data` with a `form` and `values`. |

The part is ignored when the extension is not on the stored card, the task is not input-required, the part is malformed, or it is not the latest input request. One live approval per task. The agent cannot name the reviewer or the policy.

On approval the console sends the approved content once. `metadata.approval` on that message is:

```json
{
  "approval": {
    "requestId": "<uuid>",
    "decisionId": "<uuid>",
    "revision": 1,
    "revisionDigest": "<sha-256 hex>"
  }
}
```

The digest is SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of `{ "kind", "text", "data" }` for `send_message` (`data` is null when absent) or `{ "kind", "form", "values" }` for `send_data`. Object keys are sorted at every level. A reviewer who edits the action changes the digest. Rejecting, requesting changes, or delegating does not send the action. The digest is not a signature, and Taskbay does not prove what the agent did after receiving it.

## Record, hosting, and content

| Topic | What is true |
| --- | --- |
| Durability | Commands and observations are stored in PGlite (local) or PostgreSQL before the screens read them. Closing the browser does not drop the task. |
| Hosting | You run it. Local mode has no account. A team deployment is from source, with PostgreSQL and OIDC. There is no container image or Helm chart. |
| Telemetry | The application does not send telemetry. |
| Content | Text, Markdown, JSON, CSV, and archived images, audio, video, and PDF, drawn by fixed code. Remote URLs are not loaded. |
| Audit | Append-only rows, enforced by database triggers. No built-in retention, export, or cryptographic tamper evidence. |
| Webhook | One optional notification webhook per deployment. The webhook body is HMAC-signed. That signature is not the approval. |
| Approvals | Bound to one revision and its digest. Separation of duties is on by default. An approval is a record and a trigger, not a lock: a plain reply can still be sent while one is open. |

## Python helper and examples

`sdk/python` (version 0.1.0 in the source tree) is an experimental agent helper. Classifier: Alpha. It is not on PyPI. Install from git or from a checkout:

```bash
pip install "git+https://github.com/allsrc/agent-taskbay.git#subdirectory=sdk/python"
```

```bash
pip install -e sdk/python
```

It serves `/.well-known/agent-card.json` and `/card.json`, and it emits the approval data part above. A follow-up completes the task only when `metadata.approval` matches the content that arrived. It is not a client of `/api/*`, and it does not integrate LangGraph, CrewAI, or ADK.

`examples/python-requests-taskbay` uses that helper and does open an approval.

`examples/langgraph-taskbay-adapter`, `examples/crewai-taskbay-gate`, and `examples/google-adk-taskbay-gate` are sketches. They do not open a connection. Issue 18 tracks an ADK adapter. There is no AutoGen example.

## Where it fits

| You need | What fits |
| --- | --- |
| A shared inbox, approvals, and an audit trail for A2A agents | Agent Taskbay |
| A pause inside LangGraph, ADK, or CrewAI | That framework's own mechanism. This repository does not bridge it. |
| A stable API or client SDK for other software to call the console | Not built (issue 31). |
| Cryptographic proof of the audit trail, or proof the agent executed the action | Not claimed. |
